t: You're standing near the site of Albion Mills, a steam-powered flour mill that once stood on the southeastern side of Blackfriars Bridge, in northern Southwark. Matthew Boulton began planning it as early as 1783. It was completed in 1786, and a fire gutted it in 1791. The architect was Samuel Wyatt, an English architect and engineer from the famous Wyatt family, who worked mainly in a neoclassical style. Most of the notable engineering drawings of the mill are now kept in Birmingham Central Library.
